# INC-5521: Oversold stock and stuck holds during the September flash sale

Reported by the checkout team after the 2026-09-12 flash sale.

## What we saw

- The `sneaker-limited` drop had 250 units. We confirmed 263 orders, and 13
  customers had to be refunded.
- The stock dashboard showed `reserved` going negative for two SKUs after the
  sale, and it has not recovered.
- Some customers who retried checkout after a timeout had units held twice for
  one order; the second hold only disappeared when the reservation expired.
- One order was rejected because a bundle item was out of stock, but the other
  item in the bundle stayed held until we restarted the worker pool.
- Finance reports `sold` counts that are higher than the number of orders we
  shipped for a few SKUs.

## Context

Every checkout worker calls `InventoryService` concurrently. During the sale
we ran 40 workers. The nightly `expire()` job ran once during the sale.

The unit tests all pass, and none of this reproduces when we click through
checkout by hand.

A service-wide lock (INC-5490) stopped the overselling in staging but cut
checkout throughput by 90% and was rolled back the same day.

	if [[ $# -eq 0 ]]
	then
		echo "Usage: dx <NUMBER>        (e.g. dx 999, dx ENG-999)"
		echo "       dx \"<description>\" (e.g. dx \"fix login bug\")"
		echo "       dx --session \"<prompt>\"   Open a session in the current checkout"
		echo "       dx --workflow \"<task>\"    Run the full ticket-to-PR workflow"
		echo "       dx --agent codex --model gpt-5.3-codex \"<task>\""
		echo "       dx --no-worktree <task>"
		echo "       dx --resume        Resume the most recent session"
		echo "       dx --from-pr <N>   Resume session linked to a PR"
		echo "       dx triage [ticket] Clarify, estimate, and organise tickets"

	local dx_agent_flag="" 
	local dx_model_flag=""

	do
		case "$1" in
			(--session|--workflow) if [[ -z "$dx_prompt_mode" && ${#dx_args[@]} -gt 0 ]]

				then
					dx_error "Usage: dx --agent <claude|codex> <command-or-task>"
					return 1
				fi
				dx_agent_flag="$2" 
				shift 2 ;;
			(--agent=*) dx_agent_flag="${1#--agent=}" 
				if [[ -z "$dx_agent_flag" ]]
				then
					dx_error "Usage: dx --agent <claude|codex> <command-or-task>"
					return 1
				fi
				shift ;;
			(--model) if [[ $# -lt 2 || -z "${2:-}" || "${2:-}" == --* ]]
				then
					dx_error "Usage: dx --model <model> <command-or-task>"
					return 1
				fi
				dx_model_flag="$2" 
				shift 2 ;;
			(--model=*) dx_model_flag="${1#--model=}" 
				if [[ -z "$dx_model_flag" ]]
				then
					dx_error "Usage: dx --model <model> <command-or-task>"
					return 1
				fi
				shift ;;
			(--) if [[ ${#dx_args[@]} -eq 0 ]]
				then
					dx_literal_prompt=1 
					shift
				fi
				dx_args+=("$@") 
				break ;;

				dx_workspace_flag=1 
				shift ;;
			(--worktree) use_worktree=1 
				dx_workspace_flag=1 
				shift ;;
			(*) dx_args+=("$1") 
				shift ;;
		esac
	done

	if [[ -n "$dx_agent_flag" ]]
	then
		dx_agent_flag=$(dx_agent_normalize "$dx_agent_flag")  || return 1
		local -x DX_AGENT_OVERRIDE="$dx_agent_flag" 
	fi
	if [[ -n "$dx_model_flag" ]]
	then
		dx_provider_validate_model_field "dx --model" "$dx_model_flag" || return 1
		local -x DX_MODEL_OVERRIDE="$dx_model_flag" 
	fi
	if [[ $# -eq 0 ]]
	then
		echo "Usage: dx [--agent <claude|codex>] [--model <model>] <NUMBER|description|command>"
		return 1
	fi
	local dx_command_input="$1" 
	if [[ "$dx_literal_prompt" -eq 1 || ( -n "$dx_prompt_mode" && "$1" != --help && "$1" != -h ) ]]
	then
		dx_command_input="" 
	fi
	if [[ "$dx_command_input" == "triage" || "$dx_command_input" == "refine" ]]
	then
		shift
		dxtriage "$@"
		return $?
	fi
	if [[ "$dx_command_input" == "rename" ]]
	then
		dx_error "'dx rename' is not a command. Dex names lifecycle branches during ticket setup."
		return 1
	fi
	case "$dx_command_input" in
		(init|sync|login|logout|whoami|dexcode|worker|maintain|tools|test|config|provider|setup|router|account|accounts|model|route|profile|context|run|run-gate|worktree|review|control|sessions|ps|doctor|ui-capture|research|install|uninstall|uninit|status|reload|help|--help|-h|revert|log) __dx_cli "$@"
			return $? ;;
	esac

		(dxreviewloop|dxcomplete|dxloop|dxrm|dxls|dxcd|dxclean|dxtriage|dxrefine) dx_error "'${1}' is a standalone shell command, not a 'dx' subcommand."
			dx_info "Run '${1}' directly, without the leading 'dx'. Nothing started."
			return 1 ;;
	esac
	local raw_input="${(j: :)@}" 
	if [[ -z "$raw_input" ]]
	then
		dx_error "Supply a prompt or ticket."
		return 2
	fi
	if [[ -z "$dx_prompt_mode" && "$dx_literal_prompt" -eq 0 ]]
	then
		__dx_confirm_task_word "$1" "$#" || return 1
		if [[ "$1" == --resume || "$1" == --from-pr ]] || __dx_is_ticket "$raw_input"
		then
			dx_prompt_mode=workflow 
		fi
	fi
	if [[ -z "$dx_prompt_mode" && "$dx_workspace_flag" -eq 1 ]]
	then
		dx_prompt_mode=workflow 
	fi
	if [[ -z "$dx_prompt_mode" ]]
	then
		if [[ ! -t 0 || ! -t 1 ]]
		then
			dx_error "Choose --session or --workflow for a free-form prompt without a terminal."
			return 2
		fi
		dx_prompt_mode=$(__dx_choose_prompt_mode)  || return $?
	fi
	if [[ "$dx_prompt_mode" == session ]]
	then
		if [[ "$dx_workspace_flag" -eq 1 ]]
		then
			dx_error "Workspace flags apply to --workflow. A session uses the current checkout."
			return 2
		fi
		dx_provider_session "$raw_input"
		return $?
	fi
	local -x DEX_SESSION_ONLY=0 
	__dx_refresh_provider || return 1
	if [[ "$dx_literal_prompt" -eq 0 && "$1" == "--resume" ]]
	then
		local last_session_file="$DX_STATE_DIR/last-session" 
		if [[ ! -f "$last_session_file" ]]
		then
			dx_error "No previous session found."
			dx_info "Start a new session with: dx <number>"
			return 1
		fi
		local last_info
		last_info=$(cat "$last_session_file" 2>/dev/null) 
		__dx_parse_last_session "$last_info"
		local resume_selector="session:${_dx_session_id}" 
		__dx_sessions_resume_selected "$resume_selector" "$dx_agent_flag" legacy-last-session "$_dx_wt_name" "$_dx_wt_dir" "$_dx_workspace_mode"
		return $?
	fi
	if [[ "$dx_literal_prompt" -eq 0 && "$1" == "--from-pr" ]]
	then
		if [[ -z "${2:-}" ]]
		then
			echo "Usage: dx --from-pr <PR_NUMBER|URL>"
			return 1
		fi
		local provider_prompt
		provider_prompt=$(__dx_provider_prompt) 
		local pr_args=("${DX_CLAUDE_FLAGS[@]}") 
		[[ -n "$provider_prompt" ]] && pr_args+=(--append-system-prompt "$provider_prompt") 
		pr_args+=(--from-pr "$2") 
		local session_id
		session_id="from-pr-$(dx_unique_session_id)" 
		dx_provider_cleanup_session_state "$session_id"
		DEX_SESSION_ID="$session_id" __dx_claude "${pr_args[@]}"
		local exit_code=$? 
		dx_provider_cleanup_session_state "$session_id"
		return $exit_code
	fi
	if [[ $use_worktree -eq 1 ]]
	then
		if ! __dx_setup_worktree "$raw_input"
		then
			return 1
		fi
	else
		if ! __dx_setup_in_place "$raw_input"
		then
			return 1
		fi
	fi
	local session_id state_file times_file
	session_id="$_dx_session_id" 
	state_file=$(dx_state_file "$session_id") 
	times_file=$(dx_times_file "$session_id") 
	__dx_write_last_session "$_dx_wt_name" "$_dx_wt_dir" "$_dx_workspace_mode" || dx_warn "Could not record this session for dx --resume."
	local step=0 
	if [[ -e "$state_file" || -L "$state_file" ]]
	then
		step=$(dx_lifecycle_phase_state "$session_id" 2>/dev/null)  || {
			dx_error "Dex found an unsafe or malformed authoritative phase file. Repair it before starting."
			__dx_startup_claim_release || true
			return 1
		}
	fi
	if [[ $step -gt 6 ]]
	then
		if ! dx_lifecycle_terminal_commit_valid "$session_id"
		then
			dx_error "Dex found Phase 7 without a valid terminal commit proof. The lifecycle remains inert; repair its state before treating it as complete."
			__dx_startup_claim_release || true
			return 1
		fi
		echo "Ticket lifecycle already complete for ${_dx_wt_name}."
		if [[ "$_dx_workspace_mode" == "worktree" ]]
		then
			echo "Local cleanup should already be complete. If files remain, run dxrm ${raw_input}."
		else
			echo "This lifecycle ran in the current checkout; local branch cleanup is handled at completion when safe."
		fi
		if ! __dx_startup_claim_release
		then
			return 1
		fi
		return 0
	fi
	if [[ $_dx_is_task -eq 1 ]]
	then
		mkdir -p "$DX_LOOP_DIR"
		__dx_write_state "$(dx_prompt_file "$session_id")" "$raw_input"
	fi
	if [[ $step -gt 0 ]]
	then
		echo "Resuming ${_dx_wt_name} from Phase ${step}: $(__dx_phase_name "$step")..."
	fi
	local resume_hint="dx ${raw_input}" 
	[[ $_dx_is_task -eq 1 ]] && resume_hint="dx --workflow ${(q)raw_input}" 
	[[ "$_dx_workspace_mode" == "in-place" ]] && resume_hint="dx --no-worktree ${raw_input}" 
	cd "$_dx_wt_dir" 2> /dev/null || {
		__dx_startup_claim_release || true
		return 1
	}
	__dx_run_with_runtime "$session_id" "$_dx_wt_dir" __dx_run_phases_inline "$_dx_wt_name" "$_dx_wt_dir" "$_dx_default_branch" "$step" "$state_file" "$times_file" "$resume_hint" "$_dx_workspace_mode" "$session_id" "$raw_input"
	return $?
}

# inventory-service

Stock reservations for checkout. `InventoryService` keeps three counters per
SKU (`stock`, `reserved`, `sold`) and moves orders from `reserved` to either
`committed` or `released`. The store is a key-value store with `get`, `set`
and `keys`.

```js
const { InventoryService, InsufficientStockError } = require('./src');

const inventory = new InventoryService(); // or { store, reservationTtlMs, now }
await inventory.addStock('sneaker-limited', 250);

try {
  await inventory.reserve('order-17', [{ sku: 'sneaker-limited', qty: 1 }]);
  await inventory.commit('order-17'); // or inventory.release('order-17')
} catch (err) {
  if (!(err instanceof InsufficientStockError)) throw err;
}

await inventory.expire(); // releases reservations older than the TTL
```

## INC-5521: causes and fixes

Every symptom in `ISSUE.md` came from one of two problems. Each method did
read-modify-write on store records with no mutual exclusion, and the store
yields between every read and write, so concurrent calls overwrote each
other's work. Separately, two code paths ignored an order's state.

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 263 orders confirmed on 250 units | Concurrent `reserve` calls read the same `reserved` value, and each wrote back its own increment, so all but one hold were lost. | Every write to a SKU record happens under that SKU's lock. |
| `reserved` negative after the sale | `expire()` released every order past the TTL, committed ones included, and `release()` accepted committed orders, so units that had already been sold were subtracted from `reserved` a second time. Concurrent release/commit/expire of one order could also each apply their change. | `release` rejects committed orders with `OrderStateError`, as its doc comment says. `expire` only touches orders that are still `reserved`, and re-checks under the order lock. |
| A retried checkout held units twice | `reserve` checked for an existing order, then held stock, then wrote the order. A retry that arrived before the order record existed held the stock again. | `reserve` holds the order's lock from the existence check until the record is written, so a retry waits and then returns the first reservation. |
| A rejected bundle left its other item held | `reserve` held items one by one and threw on the first short item without undoing earlier holds. No order record was written, so `expire` could never find the hold. | All items are checked under their locks before anything is written. |
| `sold` higher than shipped orders | Two concurrent `commit`s of one order both saw `reserved` and both added to `sold`. `expire` could also flip a committed order to `released` after its units were counted as sold. | `commit` runs under the order lock. `expire` skips committed orders. |

`addStock` had the same lost-update race and takes the SKU lock too.

The tests in `tests/incident-5521.test.js` reproduce each row. 17 of the 18
fail against the previous implementation. The one that passes is a
regression guard: a reservation rejected for stock must not block a retry.

## Concurrency design

`src/keyed-mutex.js` is a FIFO lock per string key. The service locks the
same keys it stores (`sku:<sku>`, `order:<orderId>`):

- `addStock` locks its SKU.
- `reserve`, `commit` and `release` lock the order, then all of the order's
  SKUs.
- `expire` reads orders without a lock to skip committed and released ones
  (both states are final). For each stale reservation it takes that order's
  lock and SKU locks, and checks the order again before releasing it.
- `available`, `snapshot`, `getItem` and `getOrder` read a single record and
  take no lock.

**No deadlocks.** A call holds at most one order lock, takes it before any
SKU lock, and takes its SKU locks in sorted order. Every call therefore
acquires locks in the same global order.

**No global lock.** Calls that share no SKU and no order never wait for each
other. INC-5490 put everything behind one lock and cut throughput by 90%;
`tests/isolation-and-recovery.test.js` stalls a call inside the store and
checks that calls on other SKUs and orders still finish.

**Lock scope.** Locks live in a `WeakMap` keyed by the store object, so two
`InventoryService` instances built on the same store also exclude each
other. Keys are dropped from the lock table once nobody holds or waits for
them, so memory tracks in-flight calls rather than the SKU catalogue.

**Hot SKUs still serialize.** Every reservation of `sneaker-limited` takes
the same lock, which is the only way to stop overselling with a store that
has no compare-and-set. The lock is held for about three store round trips
per call.

### Store failures

Counter writes happen before the order record write, so an order's status
only changes after all of its counters have. If a write rejects, the
counters already written are restored from the values read under the lock,
and the original error is rethrown. If a restore also fails, the call
rejects with an `AggregateError` listing both errors and naming the keys that
need repair. This assumes a rejected `set` did not apply.

The service sets no timeouts on store calls. A timeout that gave up the lock
while a write was still in flight would let that write land later over
someone else's update. Store call timeouts belong in the store client, where
a timed-out command actually fails.

## Behaviour changes

The public API is unchanged: same methods, arguments, return values and
error types. Three behaviours now match the doc comments where they did not
before:

- `release` of a committed order rejects with `OrderStateError`.
- `expire` releases only orders still in `reserved`, and returns only the ids
  it released on that call.
- The constructor rejects with `ValidationError` a store that lacks `get`,
  `set` or `keys`.

## Assumptions and limits

- **One process.** The locks are in-process. The incident's 40 workers are
  modelled as concurrent callers of one service, as the task states. Workers
  in separate processes against a shared Redis would need atomic operations
  in the store (`WATCH`/`MULTI` or a Lua script), which `get`/`set`/`keys`
  cannot express.
- **Existing bad data is not repaired.** SKUs whose `reserved` went negative
  in production keep their wrong counters. The correct value is the sum of
  `qty` over orders in `reserved` status for that SKU. `assertLedger` in
  `tests/helpers.js` computes that invariant and could be adapted into a
  one-off repair script.
- `expire` walks orders one at a time. It holds no lock between orders, so a
  long sweep slows no checkout call beyond the order it is working on.

## Tests

```sh
npm test
```

| File | Covers |
| --- | --- |
| `tests/inventory.test.js` | Public API behaviour, validation, TTL boundary, unicode |
| `tests/incident-5521.test.js` | One `describe` per incident symptom, plus a 40-worker flash-sale replay |
| `tests/isolation-and-recovery.test.js` | No waiting across unrelated SKUs/orders, store failure rollback, non-cloning stores, seeded random stress |
| `tests/keyed-mutex.test.js` | Lock ordering, FIFO, cleanup, deadlock freedom |

The race tests rely on the store yielding to the event loop on every call,
as `src/store.js` does. The "offset sweep" tests start a second call 0–8
store round trips after the first. Calls started at the same instant also
lose each other's writes, which can hide a double hold or double commit, so
the sweep makes the second call land at every stage of the first.

other's work. Separately, two code paths ignored an order's state.

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 263 orders confirmed on 250 units | Concurrent `reserve` calls read the same `reserved` value, and each wrote back its own increment, so all but one hold were lost. | Every write to a SKU record happens under that SKU's lock. |
| `reserved` negative after the sale | `expire()` released every order past the TTL, committed ones included, and `release()` accepted committed orders, so units that had already been sold were subtracted from `reserved` a second time. Concurrent release/commit/expire of one order could also each apply their change. | `release` rejects committed orders with `OrderStateError`, as its doc comment says. `expire` only touches orders that are still `reserved`, and re-checks under the order lock. |
| A retried checkout held units twice | `reserve` checked for an existing order, then held stock, then wrote the order. A retry that arrived before the order record existed held the stock again. | `reserve` holds the order's lock from the existence check until the record is written, so a retry waits and then returns the first reservation. |
| A rejected bundle left its other item held | `reserve` held items one by one and threw on the first short item without undoing earlier holds. No order record was written, so `expire` could never find the hold. | All items are checked under their locks before anything is written. |
| `sold` higher than shipped orders | Two concurrent `commit`s of one order both saw `reserved` and both added to `sold`. `expire` could also flip a committed order to `released` after its units were counted as sold. | `commit` runs under the order lock. `expire` skips committed orders. |

`addStock` had the same lost-update race and takes the SKU lock too.

The tests in `tests/incident-5521.test.js` reproduce each row. 17 of the 18
fail against the previous implementation. The one that passes is a
regression guard: a reservation rejected for stock must not block a retry.

## Concurrency design

`src/keyed-mutex.js` is a FIFO lock per string key. The service locks the
same keys it stores (`sku:<sku>`, `order:<orderId>`):

- `addStock` locks its SKU.
- `reserve`, `commit` and `release` lock the order, then all of the order's
  SKUs.
- `expire` reads orders without a lock to skip committed and released ones
  (both states are final). For each stale reservation it takes that order's
  lock and SKU locks, and checks the order again before releasing it.
- `available`, `snapshot`, `getItem` and `getOrder` read a single record and
  take no lock.

**No deadlocks.** A call holds at most one order lock, takes it before any
SKU lock, and takes its SKU locks in sorted order. Every call therefore
acquires locks in the same global order.

**No global lock.** Calls that share no SKU and no order never wait for each
other. INC-5490 put everything behind one lock and cut throughput by 90%;
`tests/isolation-and-recovery.test.js` stalls a call inside the store and
checks that calls on other SKUs and orders still finish.

**Lock scope.** Locks live in a `WeakMap` keyed by the store object, so two
`InventoryService` instances built on the same store also exclude each
other. Keys are dropped from the lock table once nobody holds or waits for
them, so memory tracks in-flight calls rather than the SKU catalogue.

**Hot SKUs still serialize.** Every reservation of `sneaker-limited` takes
the same lock, which is the only way to stop overselling with a store that
has no compare-and-set. The lock is held for about three store round trips
per call.

### Store failures

Counter writes happen before the order record write, so an order's status
only changes after all of its counters have. If a write rejects, the
counters already written are restored from the values read under the lock,
and the original error is rethrown. If a restore also fails, the call
rejects with an `AggregateError` listing both errors and naming the keys that
need repair. This assumes a rejected `set` did not apply.

The service sets no timeouts on store calls. A timeout that gave up the lock
while a write was still in flight would let that write land later over
someone else's update. Store call timeouts belong in the store client, where
a timed-out command actually fails.

## Behaviour changes

The public API is unchanged: same methods, arguments, return values and
error types. Three behaviours now match the doc comments where they did not
before:

- `release` of a committed order rejects with `OrderStateError`.
- `expire` releases only orders still in `reserved`, and returns only the ids
  it released on that call.
- The constructor rejects with `ValidationError` a store that lacks `get`,
  `set` or `keys`.

## Assumptions and limits

- **One process.** The locks are in-process. The incident's 40 workers are
  modelled as concurrent callers of one service, as the task states. Workers
  in separate processes against a shared Redis would need atomic operations
  in the store (`WATCH`/`MULTI` or a Lua script), which `get`/`set`/`keys`
  cannot express.
- **Existing bad data is not repaired.** SKUs whose `reserved` went negative
  in production keep their wrong counters. The correct value is the sum of
  `qty` over orders in `reserved` status for that SKU. `assertLedger` in
  `tests/helpers.js` computes that invariant and could be adapted into a
  one-off repair script.
- `expire` walks orders one at a time. It holds no lock between orders, so a
  long sweep slows no checkout call beyond the order it is working on.

## Tests

```sh
npm test
```

| File | Covers |
| --- | --- |
| `tests/inventory.test.js` | Public API behaviour, validation, TTL boundary, unicode |
| `tests/incident-5521.test.js` | One `describe` per incident symptom, plus a 40-worker flash-sale replay |
| `tests/isolation-and-recovery.test.js` | No waiting across unrelated SKUs/orders, store failure rollback, non-cloning stores, seeded random stress |
| `tests/keyed-mutex.test.js` | Lock ordering, FIFO, cleanup, deadlock freedom |

The race tests rely on the store yielding to the event loop on every call,
as `src/store.js` does. The "offset sweep" tests start a second call 0–8
store round trips after the first. Calls started at the same instant also
lose each other's writes, which can hide a double hold or double commit, so
the sweep makes the second call land at every stage of the first.

content.text:
I've fixed every problem in the incident report, and the full suite passes: 67 tests, run once through `dx run-gate --name full-gate`. Of the 18 tests that reproduce the incident, 17 fail against the old code. The one that passes there is a deliberate guard: an order rejected for stock must still be retryable.

**Causes.** Each method read a store record, changed it and wrote it back with nothing stopping other calls in between. The store pauses on every read and write, so concurrent calls overwrote each other. Two code paths also ignored an order's status.

| Symptom | Cause |
|---|---|
| 263 orders on 250 units | Concurrent `reserve` calls read the same `reserved` count, so all but one hold were lost. |
| `reserved` went negative | `expire()` released committed orders too, and `release()` accepted committed orders, so sold units were taken off `reserved` a second time. Concurrent release, commit and expire on one order made it worse. |
| Retry held units twice | `reserve` checked for an existing order before holding stock but wrote the order record last, so a retry in that gap held stock again. |
| Bundle item stayed held | `reserve` held items one at a time and threw on the short item without undoing earlier holds. No order record was written, so `expire` could never clean it up. |
| `sold` above shipped orders | Two concurrent `commit`s of one order both added to `sold`. The old `expire` also relabelled committed orders as released after they were counted as sold. |

**Fix.** I added a small per-key lock in `src/keyed-mutex.js` and use it in `src/inventory.js`:
- `reserve`, `commit` and `release` lock the order, then all of its SKUs; `addStock` locks its SKU.
- Each call takes at most one order lock, before its SKU locks, and takes SKU locks in sorted order, so calls can't deadlock.
- Calls that share no SKU and no order never wait for each other. A test stalls one call inside the store and checks that calls on other SKUs still finish; that test fails if you swap in one service-wide lock.
- `reserve` checks every item before holding any.
- `release` now rejects committed orders with `OrderStateError`, as its doc comment says.
- `expire` only releases orders still in `reserved`, and re-checks each one under its lock.
- If the store fails partway through a write, counters already written are put back, so an order is never half-applied.

The public API is unchanged and `src/store.js` is untouched. The one addition: the constructor now throws `ValidationError` if the store lacks `get`, `set` or `keys`.

**Tests** are in `tests/incident-5521.test.js`, one group per symptom plus a 40-worker flash-sale replay with a mid-sale `expire`. There are three more files: lock unit tests, isolation and store-failure tests (including a seeded random stress run), and the existing API tests with edge cases added.

**Limits** (also in `README.md`):
- **One process only.** The locks work within one process, which is how the task describes the workers. Separate worker processes sharing one Redis would need atomic operations in the store, which `get`/`set`/`keys` can't provide.
- **Existing production data is not repaired.** The two SKUs with negative `reserved` stay wrong until corrected. `reserved` can be recomputed from the order records. `sold` can't be fully rebuilt that way, because the old `expire` relabelled committed orders; shipment records would be needed. Any repair script should run with checkout paused.

The work is in four commits on `fix/inc-5521-inventory-races`, not pushed because the repo has no remote. The repo's commit hooks required conventional commit messages and a Dex co-author line, so the commits use those. `CLAUDE.md` is still untracked, as it was when I started.
